notes: Covers all five WaveSurfer 3000z models (3014z 100MHz, 3024z 200MHz, 3034z 350MHz, 3054z 500MHz, 3104z 1GHz) — physical I/O is identical across the line per the official datasheet and Getting Started Guide. Not an AV device; this is a bench oscilloscope, so category/type lists don't have a good fit ("other" used). BNC channel inputs (CH1-CH4), EXT Trigger In, AUX Out, and WaveSource Out are all 50-ohm BNC test-and-measurement signals, not video SDI, so no bandwidth "grade" applies to them (grade scale is video/data-specific per instructions). VGA output mapped to the "vga" connector id (DB-15, 1024x600 max resolution support). Ethernet is 10/100Base-T (RJ-45) so graded eth-100m (the port supports both 10 and 100 Mb/s; 100M chosen as the port's max rated speed). USB: 4 total USB 2.0 Host ports (2 front + 2 rear, USB-A, for peripherals/flash drives) graded usb-2.0; plus 1 rear USBTMC device port for remote PC control, wired via USB-A/B cable, so labeled as USB-B (device-side) per the manual's connection instructions, also graded usb-2.0. The optional 16-channel Mixed Signal digital leadset connects via a proprietary "Mixed Signal Interface" port on the front panel (a keyed ribbon/leadset connector, not a BNC) — no id in the allowed connector list matches this proprietary interface, so it is omitted from the port list rather than mis-mapped; treat the physical I/O list as slightly incomplete on that one interface. AC power inlet is a standard IEC C14 rear inlet with integrated fuse holder (universal 100-240VAC auto-sensing); cord ships per-region. Source: official Teledyne LeCroy datasheet (wavesurfer3000z_ds-20jan22, connectivity table on p.15) and official Getting Started Guide (934416-00 Rev A, labeled front/back panel diagrams on pp.4-7), both hosted on cdn.teledynelecroy.com — fully authoritative and consistent with each other.
